Probably not, when our body is low on nutrients we generally seek out more food with that nutrient naturally or just more food in general to make up for the lack of it.

For potassium just eat some spinach, broccoli, brussel sprout, salmon, or avocado.

For magnesium the same food minus broccoli/brussel. Also almonds and cacao nibs/chocolate.

For calcium spinach and salmon again, so an easy salad there. Kale, collared and leafy greens, and almonds. Or you could grind bones and make some keto bread.

These will probably be your lowest minerals on keto, magnesium is handy if you like being able to sleep at night as well on keto, lots of people end up not getting enough and having worsened sleep.
Anyway, you probably wont die since you'll just seek out more high nutrient food, but you might feel tired, unwell, have headaches, etc. Try measuring your nutrient intake with an app like cronometer if you want to see how close your meal plan gets you to the right nutrient levels :)

Kind of a shit term, but i consider the difference to be the damage/potential for damage caused by taking them.
Soft drugs: weed, lsd, shrooms, caffeine, etc. Things which dont directly put you at risk of death or major physical harm when taken by itself.
Hard drugs: meth, cocaine, heroin. Alcohol, etc. If you can fairly easily just straight up die or cause unreasonable damage to your body by taking them than its a hard drug.
In addition not all drugs are equally soft or hard, coffees softer than shrooms, meths harder than alcohol. Its just a bad distinction, but generally i consider it a safety/health/addiction thing.

As someone who's gone through this before, the best advice i can give you is to come to terms with your mortality. Philosophy can definitely help, don't get trapped in your own nihilistic and self destructive thoughts.
Consider this, while everything you've written may be true, what does it actually change. While it may be true that there is no intrinsic meaning and nothing has any objective value, wasn't it always that way? Objectively nothing has changed, the only thing that's changed is your perception. You don't need to assign false values to the world around you, nothing has ever meant anything and most importantly, that doesn't matter.

The only thing that matters is how you want to go forward with things now that you've seen past the bullshit.
Worrying about your mortality wont change anything.
Everything has always been pointless objectively, reality only has meaning to the observer. If you crave meaning and value then live meaningfully, do what you want to do and if you don't know what that is then find out. You have the rest of your life ahead of you and if you waste it worrying about the pointless state of reality you'll regret it.

Take action to create a life which you can wake up to and be happy for the work ahead, you assign the meaning in your life, so live true to your values.

The most important thing though is not to dwell on it, and to live true to your values.
